interest: Shows SCAP's postwar price controls on perishable foods, tying compliance to continued petroleum and fertilizer imports.
overview: This file (894.5017, May 29, 1946 – June 23, 1948) documents economic controls, commodity pricing, and food distribution in occupied Japan. It opens with a May 1946 State Department communication to the British Embassy establishing an equitable export ceiling price and quality grade for Japanese stockpiles of antimony. The remainder of the file, spanning December 1947 to June 1948, centers on the enforcement of strict price caps and rationing schemes for perishable foodstuffs—primarily fish and vegetables—overseen by the Price Control and Rationing Division of SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section. Through diplomatic despatches, public press statements, and the formal issuance of SCAPIN 1910 under Directive No. 3, the file illustrates occupation efforts to curb rampant inflation, stamp out food black markets, and secure equitable food distribution among the Japanese public.

subfiles.about: Informs the British Embassy of the quality grade and agreed ceiling price for exportable Japanese antimony stockpiles.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Japanese and Korean Economic Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman sets a price for Japanese antimony stocks after confirming their purity with SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Douglass Campbell regarding Japanese Antimony Stocks and Ceiling Price
subfiles.to: Douglass Campbell, Raw Materials Section, British Embassy, Washington, D. C.

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP public statements on newly established price and distribution controls over perishable foods in Japan.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP officials announce new price and rationing controls on fish and vegetables, widely published in Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1467 from the Acting Political Adviser for Japan regarding Statements on Price Control and Rationing of Perishable Foods

subfiles.about: Publicizes a speech by SCAP official N. A. Stitt urging Tokyo fish and vegetable retailers to support price control enforcement.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.summary: SCAP's Stitt tells Tokyo food dealers their compliance is key to enforcing perishable-food controls beyond staple rice.
subfiles.title: SCAP Press Release: Statement by N. A. Stitt to Vegetable and Fish Dealers on Enforcement Campaign

subfiles.about: Articulates SCAP's policy rationale for maintaining strict price caps and rationing on fish and vegetables to combat black markets and inflation.
subfiles.from: H. F. Alber, Chief, Price Control & Rationing Division, Economic & Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.summary: SCAP's Alber defends strict fish and vegetable controls, citing a disastrous 1945 decontrol and warning farmers their fuel and fertilizer imports depend on avoiding black markets.
subfiles.title: Press Conference Statement by H. F. Alber on Control of Fish and Vegetables
subfiles.to: Press conference attendees and general public

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1910 confirming that fish and vegetables are classified as essential commodities in short supply subject to mandatory controls.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1910 reaffirms fish and vegetables as essential controlled commodities under 1945's Directive No. 3.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 382 from the Acting Political Adviser for Japan regarding Price and Distribution Controls Over Fish and Vegetables

subfiles.about: Formally directs the Japanese Government to maintain price and distribution controls over fish and vegetables under Directive No. 3.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (by Colonel R. M. Levy, Adjutant General)
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1910 designates fish and vegetables as essential commodities under Directive No. 3, mandating continued price and distribution controls.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1910: Memorandum for the Japanese Government on Price and Distribution Controls Over Fish and Vegetables
